subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin/API-level pre-persistence config write veto hook, and what ordering, failure, and metadata contract should it use?
rationale: This changes a public plugin/config security boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent hook contract or failure semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add a guarded config-write hook
options.body: Define a single synchronous interception seam after built-in validation and SecretRef preflight but before persistence, with current/pending config, action, raw payload, baseHash, actor metadata, changed paths, and typed rejection.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight work
options.body: Keep #9993 open but make the broader plugin preflight framework own the final hook contract and ordering.

options.title: Keep built-in validation only
options.body: Decline the plugin veto surface and document external validators as advisory wrappers, leaving config-guard bypassable by direct gateway writes.

recommendation.title: Add a guarded config-write hook
recommendation.body: Define a single synchronous interception seam after built-in validation and SecretRef preflight but before persistence, with current/pending config, action, raw payload, baseHash, actor metadata, changed paths, and typed rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the keep-open product-routing review and tied this issue to the config validation/mutation RFC direction.
